text:
alex_ng: Heads-up — seeing tail-latency spikes against the eu-west shared GPU pool for the past ~6h. Spikes line up with big egress bursts from tenant-B and a sharp rise in KV cache misses.

mira_dev: Do you have the query/graph? is it per-GPU or per-pod?

alex_ng: quick graphs: CPU ok, but per-GPU egress (MB/s) and kernel net-err counters jump. KV miss rate goes from ~2% -> 18% during spikes.

alex_ng: command I used: `curl -s "$CONSOLE/api/metrics?pool=eu-west-shared&range=6h" | jq .` and then plotted per_gpu.egress_bytes/s and kvstore.miss_rate

ops-bot: ALERT: eu-west-shared tail_latency_95p > 450ms (duration 00:32) — auto-notify sent to #eng-infra

sam_ops: Possible culprit: we pushed a soft-affinity tweak last week that pins small tenants to a subset of nodes to avoid cross-tenant KV thrash — but if one tenant bursts egress it can saturate NICs on that subset.

mira_dev: ah interesting — that would explain pod-local KV cache thrash. soft-affinity intended to reduce xfers but now concentrating noisy egress.

jun_infra: We have a scheduler flag `scheduler.soft_spill_to_shared` and per-tenant `egress_profile` that can be used to relax sticking. Suggest temporarily relaxing Tenant-B to `soft` -> `spill` for the retry window. Ramp plan below.

jun_infra: PATCH plan (pseudo):
```
# set tenant-B to spill to general pool when egress > 80MB/s
POST /api/tenants/tenant-b/config {"egress_profile":"spill","spill_threshold_mb":80}
# relax scheduler stickiness
kubectl patch configmap allocator --patch '{"data":{"soft_affinity_weight":"0.3"}}'
```

priya_sre: Two operational notes: 1) if we relax affinity, KV cache locality will drop — expect a transient increase in token generation latency for tenant-B. 2) we should add egress shaping as a safety net (tc htb token bucket) before broad unpinning.

sam_ops: Agree on shaping. We can push a qdisc rule onto affected nodes as immediate mitigation: `tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root tbf rate 400mbit burst 32kb latency 50ms` to cap bursts.

alex_ng: Cost/impact check: If we spill tenant-B to shared, we estimate ~17% uplift in shared egress cost (short-term) but avoid a 2% reserved-pool underutilization penalty and prevent customer SLO violations. I lean to try a canary tonight in lower-load window.

mira_dev: +1. Suggest canary 1% of tenant-B traffic -> spill + shaping, monitor 95/99p latencies, kv miss, and egress cost delta. Automate rollback if 95p > 600ms for >5m.

jun_infra: I'll prepare the allocator roll with feature-flag `spill-canary-tenant-b` and a revert playbook. Policy to run for 60m then evaluate.

alex_ng: I'll run the canary at 23:00 CET (deploy window) and own the runbook. tagging @mira_dev @priya_sre for monitoring. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

priya_sre: ACK — I'll watch logs and page if rollback needed. Also adding an alert: `kv.miss_rate_increase > 5pct AND tail_latency_95p > 200ms -> page oncall`.

ops-bot: Deployment scheduled by alex_ng for 2026-03-20T22:00:00Z (canary: tenant-b 1%). Rollout ID: rollout-20260320-23-tnb-spill

sam_ops: After canary, let's also evaluate a longer-term change: soften default soft-affinity heuristic to consider NIC headroom and egress variance so we avoid concentration. I'll open a design doc.

alex_ng: thanks all — will report back with canary results.
